title: Impact Aid Coronavirus Relief Act
official_summary:
Impact Aid Coronavirus Relief Act

This bill revises the Impact Aid Program application process for FY2022. It also revises FY2021 allocations under the Migrant Education Program.

First, the bill requires local educational agencies (LEAs) participating in the Impact Aid Program to use the student count or federal property valuation data from their FY2021 program applications, as applicable, for their FY2022 program applications. The program provides funding to LEAs that have lost property tax revenue due to the presence of tax-exempt federal property or to those that have experienced increased expenditures due to enrollment of federally connected children (e.g., children living on Indian lands or military bases).

In addition, the bill directs the Department of Education to use school year 2018-2019 data or school year 2019-2020 data, whichever is greater, for making FY2021 allocations to states under the Migrant Education Program. States use these program funds to identify eligible migratory children and provide them with education and support services.

summary.headline: This law lets school districts reuse their 2021 federal Impact Aid data for 2022 applications and changes how 2021 Migrant Education funds are calculated.
summary.what_it_does: Impact Aid helps school districts that lose local property tax money because federal land is tax-exempt, or that pay more to educate children connected to federal property such as military bases or Indian lands. This law requires those districts to use their FY2021 student counts or federal property values when they apply for FY2022 funds. It also tells the Department of Education to use either the 2018-2019 or 2019-2020 school year data, whichever is higher, when figuring FY2021 Migrant Education allocations to states. States use Migrant Education money to find eligible migratory children and provide them with education and support services.

who_it_affects.group: School districts that receive Impact Aid
who_it_affects.how: They must base their FY2022 applications on the student counts or federal property valuation data they reported for FY2021.
States receive Migrant Education funding for FY2021 calculated from the higher of two earlier school years, which can affect services available to eligible migratory students.
They receive FY2021 Migrant Education allocations recalculated under the higher-of-two-years rule.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 4, 2020, and applies to FY2021 Migrant Education allocations and FY2022 Impact Aid applications.
